name: std::vector reserve() preallocation (book companion code)
listed_description: Calling reserve() on a std::vector before a push_back loop avoids repeated reallocations and speeds up insertion compared with the same loop without reserve.
claim_text: Book output shows 0.01195 s without reserve versus 0.003685 s with reserve; the book says reserve was more than 3x faster.
book_benchmark: 100,000 int push_back calls on std::vector<int>, timed once with std::chrono::high_resolution_clock, with and without reserve(100000). Compiler, flags and CPU not stated; single run, no repetitions.
found_in: book: Data Structures and Algorithms with the C++ STL (2024), ch. 3, section Resizing and reserving memory / Enter reserve()
